body_markdown:
Consumers who recently purchased Horizon Organic chocolate milk from major retailers such as Target, Walmart, or Whole Foods may want to check the products in their refrigerators. Horizon Organic Dairy has recalled tens of thousands of cases of its 1% chocolate milk because of concerns that some products could be spoiled.


According to information reported by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the recall involves **53,760 cases of Horizon Organic 1% Chocolate Milk** packaged in tetra pak cartons. The company voluntarily withdrew the products after identifying a potential spoilage issue.


## Horizon Organic Milk Recall Affects More Than 53,000 Cases


The recalled products include two different case sizes. Horizon Organic Dairy withdrew approximately **19,236 cases containing 18 cartons** and another **34,524 cases containing 12 cartons** .


The products are Horizon Organic 1% Chocolate Milk, a low-fat organic chocolate milk product commonly sold in individual cartons. The milk was available through major retailers, including Target, Walmart, and Whole Foods.


The company said the product has the potential to be spoiled. Consumers should therefore avoid drinking the recalled milk until they have confirmed that their products are not included in the recall.


The expiration dates associated with the recalled products range from **January 28, 2027, through February 3, 2027** .


The recall was originally initiated on August 7, 2026. On September 8, the FDA classified the recall as a **Class II recall** , increasing the level of attention surrounding the affected products.


## What Does an FDA Class II Recall Mean?


An FDA Class II recall does not necessarily mean that a product is expected to cause severe or life-threatening illness. Instead, the classification is used when exposure to a recalled product could result in temporary or medically reversible health consequences, or when the possibility of serious health effects is considered remote.


The FDA uses three primary recall classifications.


A **Class I recall** is the most serious category. It applies when there is a reasonable likelihood that using or being exposed to a product could result in serious health consequences or death.


A **Class II recall** involves products that could potentially cause temporary or medically reversible health problems. The recalled Horizon Organic chocolate milk falls into this category.


A **Class III recall** generally involves products that are unlikely to cause adverse health consequences. Examples can include certain regulatory or labeling violations.


The classification provides consumers with additional information about the potential level of risk associated with a recalled product.


## What Should Consumers Do With Recalled Horizon Milk?


Anyone who purchased Horizon Organic 1% Chocolate Milk should check the packaging and expiration date before consuming it.


If the product matches the details associated with the recall, consumers should not drink it. Instead, they should follow instructions provided by the retailer or manufacturer regarding disposal or possible refunds.


Consumers should also avoid relying solely on the appearance or smell of the milk to determine whether it is safe. A recalled food product should be handled according to official recall instructions, even if it appears normal.


People who believe they became sick after consuming a recalled product should consider contacting a healthcare professional, particularly if they experience persistent or concerning symptoms.


## This Is Not Horizon's First Chocolate Milk Recall


The latest recall is not the first time Horizon Organic Dairy has faced a recall involving its chocolate milk products.


Earlier in 2026, the FDA reported another voluntary recall involving select sizes of Horizon Organic Chocolate Lowfat Milk with DHA Omega-3.


That earlier recall involved more than **3,500 cases of 18 cartons** , with the products packaged in 8-ounce cartons and six-pack configurations. The affected milk carried UPC **742365004322** .


The products involved in that earlier recall were distributed in **Arizona, California, Nevada, and Oregon** and had expiration dates of August 14 and August 15.


The reason for that recall was different from the latest spoilage concern. The FDA reported that the earlier products had an issue involving package integrity.


## Previous Horizon Recall Involved Packaging Problems


In a subsequent FDA enforcement report, the earlier Horizon recall was associated with concerns that compromised seals could cause packages to become bloated or leak.


A damaged or compromised package can create food safety and quality concerns, which is why consumers are generally advised not to consume products with leaking, swollen, or otherwise damaged packaging.


The earlier Horizon recall was eventually terminated on July 31, according to FDA enforcement information.


While the earlier incident involved packaging integrity, the current recall focuses on the potential for the product to be spoiled. Consumers should therefore treat the two recalls as separate events and check the specific product information associated with the current recall.


## Other Chocolate Milk Recalls Have Also Occurred


Horizon Organic is not the only dairy producer to have faced a chocolate milk recall.


In 2025, the FDA reported a recall involving **75,566 half-pint units of chocolate milk** produced by Meadow Gold Dairies Hawaii in Hilo, Hawaii.


That recall involved flavored Grade A pasteurized homogenized milk and was associated with potential quality control concerns.


The product was sold in Hawaii and contained ingredients including nonfat milk, sugar cane, cocoa processed with alkali, corn starch, carrageenan, salt, natural flavor, vitamin A palmitate, and vitamin D3.


The Meadow Gold recall began on October 14, 2025, before receiving a Class II classification from the FDA on November 28, 2025.


Meadow Gold's products are sold through retailers including Safeway, Walmart, and 7-Eleven Hawaii.


## Why Food Recalls Matter for Consumers


Food recalls are an important part of the country's food safety system. Manufacturers and regulators can use recalls to remove potentially problematic products from store shelves and consumers' homes.


For shoppers, the most important step is to pay attention to recall notices and compare the product information with items already purchased.


Consumers should check the brand name, product type, package size, expiration date, UPC code when available, and any other identifying information included in an official recall announcement.


Because recalled products may remain in household refrigerators or freezers after being removed from stores, checking products at home can be just as important as noticing recall notices at a retailer.


## Bottom Line


The latest **Horizon Organic chocolate milk recall affects 53,760 cases** of Horizon Organic 1% Chocolate Milk sold through major retailers, including Target, Walmart, and Whole Foods.


The products were recalled because of concerns that they could be spoiled, with expiration dates ranging from January 28 to February 3, 2027. The FDA has classified the recall as a Class II event.


Consumers who have Horizon Organic 1% Chocolate Milk at home should carefully check their products against the official recall information before drinking them. If a product is part of the recall, it should not be consumed.
